meta.scope: Starter set of well-documented interaction warnings taken from FDA labeling. It is NOT exhaustive. Absence of a match never means a combination is safe.

severityLevels.avoid: The label says not to use together, or lists the combination as a contraindication.
severityLevels.major: The label describes a serious risk and calls for caution. Ask a doctor or pharmacist before combining.
severityLevels.monitor: The label says the combination may cause a problem and advises monitoring or checking with a clinician.

interactions.summary: Taking an NSAID pain reliever with warfarin can raise the risk of bleeding.
interactions.why: NSAIDs can interfere with platelets and can cause stomach bleeding or ulcers, which adds to warfarin's blood-thinning effect.
interactions.action: Do not start an NSAID (ibuprofen, naproxen, etc.) without asking the doctor who manages your warfarin, or your pharmacist. Ask what to use for pain instead.

interactions.summary: Aspirin taken with warfarin can raise the risk of bleeding.
interactions.why: Aspirin can inhibit platelet aggregation and can cause stomach bleeding, ulcers, or perforation.
interactions.action: Do not add or stop aspirin on your own. The warfarin label tells patients to check with their doctor before taking other medicines, including aspirin products.

interactions.summary: Metronidazole (an antibiotic often used for dental and other infections) can strengthen the effect of warfarin.
interactions.why: The label says it can prolong clotting time, so bleeding risk can go up unless blood tests (PT/INR) are watched closely.
interactions.action: Tell whoever prescribes metronidazole that you take warfarin, and ask whether your INR needs checking.

interactions.summary: Aspirin with apixaban (Eliquis) can raise the risk of bleeding.
interactions.why: The label says drugs that affect clotting, including aspirin, increase the risk of bleeding when taken with apixaban.
interactions.action: Do not add aspirin without checking with your prescriber.

interactions.summary: NSAID pain relievers with apixaban (Eliquis) can raise the risk of bleeding.
interactions.why: The label lists NSAIDs among drugs that increase the risk of bleeding when taken with apixaban, and tells patients to mention aspirin or NSAIDs to their clinicians.
interactions.action: Ask your prescriber or pharmacist what pain reliever is appropriate before taking an NSAID.

interactions.summary: NSAID pain relievers with clopidogrel (Plavix) increase the risk of stomach and intestinal bleeding.
interactions.why: The label states that taking them together increases the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding.
interactions.action: Check with your prescriber or pharmacist before using an NSAID.

source.title: Plavix (clopidogrel) prescribing information
source.note: 2019 label version. Check for a newer one.

interactions.summary: Clopidogrel (Plavix) together with warfarin increases the risk of bleeding.
interactions.why: The two drugs affect clotting in independent ways, so the risks add up.
interactions.action: This combination is sometimes prescribed on purpose. Make sure every prescriber knows you take both.

source.title: Plavix (clopidogrel) prescribing information

interactions.summary: SSRI antidepressants taken with clopidogrel (Plavix) may increase the risk of bleeding.
interactions.why: The label says SSRIs may increase the risk of bleeding when taken with clopidogrel.
interactions.action: Make sure both prescribers know about both medicines. Do not stop either one without medical advice.

interactions.action: Make sure both prescribers know about both medicines. Do not stop either one without medical advice.

interactions.summary: Omeprazole (Prilosec) can make clopidogrel (Plavix) work less well.
interactions.why: The label says omeprazole significantly reduces clopidogrel's antiplatelet activity, and advises avoiding the combination.
interactions.action: Ask your prescriber or pharmacist about a different stomach-acid medicine.

interactions.summary: Opioid pain medicines taken with benzodiazepines can cause profound sedation, slowed breathing, coma, and death.
interactions.why: FDA required labeling changes warning about this risk and recommending the combination only when there are no adequate alternatives.
interactions.action: Tell every prescriber about both. Do not combine them or add alcohol unless your prescriber has specifically planned it.

interactions.summary: Tramadol with an SSRI antidepressant can cause serotonin syndrome and raises seizure risk.
interactions.why: The tramadol label warns that serotonin syndrome, which can be life-threatening, has occurred with serotonergic drugs, and that SSRIs raise seizure risk.
interactions.action: Ask your prescriber or pharmacist before combining. Seek urgent care for agitation, fever, fast heartbeat, muscle twitching, or confusion.

source.note: MedLibrary mirror of the FDA label text. Confirm against DailyMed.

interactions.summary: Tramadol with an SNRI antidepressant can cause serotonin syndrome.
interactions.why: The tramadol label lists SNRIs among the serotonergic drugs associated with life-threatening serotonin syndrome.
interactions.action: Ask your prescriber or pharmacist before combining. Seek urgent care for agitation, fever, fast heartbeat, muscle twitching, or confusion.

interactions.summary: Sildenafil must not be taken with nitrate medicines. The combination can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure.
interactions.why: The sildenafil label lists nitrates as a contraindication because sildenafil strengthens their blood-pressure-lowering effect.
interactions.action: Do not take them together. If you have chest pain after taking sildenafil, tell emergency staff you took it.

interactions.summary: NSAID pain relievers can weaken lisinopril's blood-pressure effect and may worsen kidney function.
interactions.why: The label says NSAIDs may reduce lisinopril's effect and may cause kidney function to worsen, especially in older people, people on water pills, or people with kidney problems.
interactions.action: Ask your prescriber or pharmacist before regular NSAID use. Kidney function may need to be checked.
